1. 원역사 & 족장 시대: 1. Primeval History & the Age of the Patriarchs
하나님께서 무에서 유를 창조하신 우주 만물의 시작과 인류의 타락을 다루는: This is the majestic prologue covering the beginning of the whole universe, which God created out of nothing, and the fall of humanity. The blessing of the Garden of Eden was shattered by human pride and disobedience, and the corruption of a world led by the descendants of Cain finally brought on a global catastrophe: the judgment of the great Flood in Noah's day. Yet even after the Flood, human pride remained, as people built the Tower of Babel to avoid being scattered. In the middle of this hopeless history, God calls Abraham, the son of an idol worshiper in Ur of the Chaldeans, and commands him, 'Go to the land that I will show you.' This single calling becomes the great first step of humanity's redemptive history. The intense and very human life stories of the four generations of patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph, show in raw detail how God, who never gives up on them even though they are full of failure and weakness, faithfully fulfills His covenant. The book of Job, written in this period against the rough wilderness backdrop of the patriarchal age, teaches God's absolute sovereignty and His plan through the laments of a righteous man struggling in suffering that seems to have no reason.
노우호 목사님의 성경강좌에서 창세기는 모든 교리와 역사의 모판입니다! 아: In Pastor Woo-ho Noh's Bible course, Genesis is the seedbed of all doctrine and history! The genealogy from Adam to Abraham is not a mere list of names; it stands for the holy seed of redemptive history that survived even through death and despair. Why did God choose Abraham and not some other people? Not because he was perfect, but in order to train him thoroughly and make him the ancestor of a 'kingdom of priests' that would show God's rule to the world. Only when you read Job inserted into the patriarchal age of Genesis can you truly grasp the world of that time, the faith of the ancients, and the pattern of the suffering of the cross that does not waver even under Satan's accusations.
Four hundred years had passed since they fell into slavery in Egypt under a new dynasty that did not know Joseph. God heard the groaning of the people of Israel, steeped to the bone in a slave mentality, and called Moses, an old man of eighty, in the wilderness of Midian. Escaping Egypt through the ten plagues and the blood of the Passover lamb, Israel experienced the miracle of crossing the Red Sea as if on dry land. Then God came down on Mount Sinai, made a covenant with them in blood, and gave them the Ten Commandments and the tabernacle system, raising their spiritual status from mere refugees to a 'holy kingdom of priests.' But because of their unbelief at Kadesh Barnea, even with the land flowing with milk and honey right before their eyes, they wandered in the wilderness for 38 years and were disciplined until the whole old generation had died. At last, standing on the plains of Moab, Moses poured out his heart, as if spitting blood, in a farewell sermon to the next generation, and that is the book of Deuteronomy.
출애굽기에서 구원받은 백성이 어떻게 살아야 하는지 그 세밀한 삶의 규칙을: The book that writes down the detailed rules of life for how the people saved in Exodus should live is none other than 'Leviticus.' If you skip Leviticus, your Bible read-through will fail! Leviticus is not just about sacrificial laws; it is a practical constitution covering hygiene, food, sexual morality, and economic justice for a people who would walk with a holy God. Numbers is a notebook of wrong answers showing how people fall in the wilderness when they disobey, and the 'Shema (Hear, O Israel)' of Deuteronomy 6 is the command to teach God's word diligently to your children; it becomes the absolute standard that decides the rise and fall of Israel's history from then on.
3. 가나안 정복 & 사사 시대: 3. The Conquest of Canaan & the Age of the Judges
모세의 뒤를 이은 여호수아의 영도 아래 이스라엘은 요단강을 건너 여리고: Under the leadership of Joshua, who succeeded Moses, Israel crosses the Jordan River, brings down the walls of Jericho, drives out the inhabitants, and divides the promised land among the twelve tribes. Up to this point it was one miracle and act of obedience after another. But when Joshua and the elders who had known that era died, Israel sank into 'another generation' that did not know God. The people, having forgotten God's law, fell deep into Baal and Asherah, the Canaanite gods of fertility and pleasure, and everyone did what was right in his own eyes, that is, lived as instinct and greed led them. It was a pitch-dark age of spiritual darkness in which the tragic cycle of 'corruption - judgment (oppression) - crying out - deliverance through a judge - corruption again' repeated without end for 350 years. Yet even at the very bottom of that darkness and corruption, the small and beautiful book of Ruth warmly shows how, through the deep loving-kindness (hesed) of Ruth the Moabite woman and through Boaz, the house of David, and beyond it the line of Jesus Christ, was being prepared.
사사 시대의 끔찍한 비극은 단 한 가지, 바로 신명기 6장의 '신앙 전수: The horrible tragedy of the age of the Judges comes down to one thing: the 'passing on of faith (the Shema)' commanded in Deuteronomy 6 failed completely! The incident of the Levite's concubine in the last part of Judges exposes in raw detail what kind of terrible monsters children become when they are not taught God's word. In that hopeless age, the shining book of Ruth shows how even a foreign woman, when she obeyed the spirit of the law (the kinsman-redeemer, the go'el system), received the honor of becoming David's grandmother, and it serves as a sharp indictment of the corrupt religious leaders.
사사 시대의 혼란을 끝내고자 이스라엘은 열방처럼 '왕'을 요구합니다. 초: To end the chaos of the age of the Judges, Israel demands a 'king' like the other nations. The first king, Saul, began humbly but soon grew proud and was rejected, and after a 40-year reign he met a miserable end on Mount Gilboa. After him David, a man after God's own heart, took the throne and reigned for 40 years, achieving the largest territory and the greatest revival in Israel's history. God made the Davidic covenant (2 Samuel 7) with David, promising an 'everlasting throne.' Under David's son Solomon, along with the building of the temple, wisdom, wealth, and glory reached their peak. But in his later years Solomon took many foreign women as wives, built high places, and sank into the swamp of idolatry. The wisest man fell into becoming the most foolish, and so the deadly tragedy of the kingdom's division was conceived. In this period of dazzling revival and downfall, Israel's praise and wisdom literature burst into full bloom.
시편 150편 중 대부분은 평안할 때 지어진 것이 아니라, 다윗이 사울을: Most of the 150 Psalms were not written in times of peace; they are cries and praises poured out in the bitter, tear-soaked places of suffering, as David fled from Saul and was chased by his son Absalom. Solomon left his deep love with God in his youth in the Song of Songs and the wisdom of ruling in his prime in Proverbs, but in old age, after ruining everything through idolatry, he wrote Ecclesiastes, full of the emptiness of life and thorough repentance. Only when you connect the poetry and wisdom books, era by era, to the History books (Samuel, Kings) can you feel the real weight of these words.
5. 분열왕국 & 선지자들의 활동: 5. The Divided Kingdom & the Ministry of the Prophets
솔로몬의 타락과 르호보암의 어리석음으로 말미암아 이스라엘은 남유다(두 지: Because of Solomon's corruption and Rehoboam's foolishness, Israel is shattered into southern Judah (two tribes) and northern Israel (ten tribes). Northern Israel never once turned back from the sin of golden-calf idolatry set up by its first king, Jeroboam. Amid endless coups and assassinations, it ignored the burning warnings of great prophets such as Elijah, Elisha, Amos, and Hosea, and finally in B.C. 722 it was wiped out of history forever by the brutal Assyrian Empire. Southern Judah, too, despite the religious reforms of good kings like Hezekiah and Josiah who walked in the way of David, could not escape God's wrath because of the monstrous idolatry and the shedding of innocent blood committed in the time of Manasseh. Jeremiah, the weeping prophet, cried out until he was spitting blood that 'surrendering to Babylon is the only way to live,' but Judah, deceived by the empty words of false prophets who said all was well, kept on rebelling to the very end, and in B.C. 586 the temple in Jerusalem was burned, the walls were torn down, and the people were dragged off miserably to Babylon.
이 시기가 에스라 성경강좌의 심장부입니다! 열왕기하의 무미건조해 보이는: This period is the heart of the Ezra Bible Course! Read the 16 prophetic books by fitting them into their exact historical setting and situation within the seemingly dry historical records of 2 Kings. The prophets' writings are not philosophy written in a back room. They are tear-soaked warning letters, cried out at the risk of their lives on the edge of the cliff, as Assyria's army closed in and the nation was collapsing! You must read in them how much God beat His chest in pain over an age that kept only religious forms and threw away justice and loving-kindness: that 'wounded heart of God.'
예루살렘의 멸망은 끝이 아니었습니다. 성전은 불탔고, 왕족과 귀족들은 눈: The fall of Jerusalem was not the end. The temple was burned, and the royal family and nobles, their eyes put out, were carried off bound in ropes to faraway Babylon. Lamentations sings of the prophet's bitter grief as he looks at Jerusalem turned to ashes. But these 70 years of exile were not meant to destroy Israel; they were God's hot furnace of refining, to filter out spiritual impurities. Daniel and his three friends, taken to the royal court of Babylon at the center of the empire, refused the food offered to idols and kept their faith in the LORD pure, and before pagan kings they proclaimed the rise and fall of world empires and the victory of God's everlasting kingdom. Meanwhile, among the despairing exiles taken to the forced camps by the river Chebar, the prophet Ezekiel proclaimed Israel's glorious restoration through the vision of dry bones becoming an army and the vision of a new temple with living water flowing out of it. It became clear that God is not someone shut up inside the temple, but the sovereign of the whole universe, present with His exiled people in a foreign land.
포로 시대는 징계인 동시에 극진한 사랑의 치유 기간이었습니다! 예루살렘에: The Exile was discipline, and at the same time a period of healing by tender love! A people who could not quit idolatry in Jerusalem were thoroughly trained in a foreign land, and only then were reborn as a people who studied the word and gathered in synagogues to pray. Through Daniel we must see that the beastlike empires of this world will surely perish and that the kingdom of Christ, the stone cut out without hands, will last forever; and through Ezekiel we must see the mighty work of the Holy Spirit who brings to life the dry bones of our broken spirits.
7. 포로 귀환 & 성전·성벽 재건: 7. The Return from Exile & Rebuilding the Temple and Walls
예레미야의 70년 예언대로, 페르시아 제국의 고레스 왕이 유대인들의 귀환: Just as Jeremiah's 70-year prophecy said, King Cyrus of the Persian Empire issues a miraculous decree ordering the Jews' return and the rebuilding of the temple. The people of the first return, led by governor Zerubbabel and the high priest Jeshua, face the trial of having temple construction halted by the opposition of the Samaritans, but through the fiery urging of the prophets Haggai and Zechariah they finally complete the Second Temple. Meanwhile, in the palace of Susa in Persia, the miracle of Purim takes place: through Esther's fasting and prayer, at the risk of her life, the Jewish people are saved from annihilation. After this, through the second return led by Ezra the scribe, a revival movement of the word arises, and through the third return led by governor Nehemiah, the walls of Jerusalem are rebuilt in 52 days. When all the building is finished, Ezra reads the Book of the Law before the people gathered in the square before the Water Gate, and a great revival breaks out as all the people weep and repent. But as time passes, faith falls back into routine, and the prophet Malachi rebukes the corrupt priests who offer sick animals as sacrifices and prophesies the messenger of the LORD who will come on the great and dreadful day, closing the door of the Old Testament.
이 시대가 바로 '에스라하우스' 사역의 뿌리이자 모델입니다! 에스라 7장: This era is the very root and model of the ministry of 'Ezra House'! Ezra 7:10: 'For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.' However splendidly you rebuild the building, if God's word is not inside it, it is an empty shell. Like the Bible conference in the square before the Water Gate in Nehemiah 8, the Korean church today can live only by returning to the original form of the word and experiencing a true revival in which people read the Bible rightly, weep, and repent.
신구약중간사 교재 (다니엘 8, 11장 예언 성취): Intertestamental Period textbook (fulfillment of the prophecies in Daniel 8 and 11)
말라기 선지자 이후 세례 요한이 광야에서 외치기 전까지, 무려 400년: After the prophet Malachi, until John the Baptist cried out in the wilderness, there was a spiritual period of silence lasting a full 400 years, in which God's official revelation and the voice of the prophets were cut off. But history never stopped. The Persian Empire fell, the Greek empire of Alexander the Great swept across the world, and Greek became the common language of the world. Under the Ptolemaic dynasty the Old Testament was translated into Greek, completing the Septuagint (LXX), and through the Maccabean revolt, which rose up against the brutal religious persecution of the Seleucid dynasty, the Jews set up the independent Hasmonean dynasty. In the end even this was conquered by the Roman general Pompey, and they came under Rome's iron rule. Through these bloody, turbulent years, various factions arose within Judaism: the Pharisees, who insisted on strict observance of the law; the Sadducees, a priestly group that had made deals with those in power; the Zealots, who waged an armed struggle for independence; and the Essenes, who withdrew into the wilderness.
노우호 목사님의 독보적인 통독 원리 중 하나가 바로 이 '신구약 중간사: One of Pastor Woo-ho Noh's unique principles of reading through the Bible is to fully grasp this '400-year Intertestamental Period'! If you jump straight from the Old Testament to the New without knowing these 400 years of history, you can never properly understand the synagogues that suddenly appear, the Roman governor Pontius Pilate, or the debates over the law between the Pharisees and the Sadducees. To human eyes it looked like a dark age in which God was silent, but in fact it was a time of God's great providence, when He was carefully setting up, without a gap, the perfect stage for Paul's missionary journeys and the spreading of the gospel, through Greek as a common world language and the highways Rome had built.
9. 예수 그리스도의 생애 & 사복음서: 9. The Life of Jesus Christ & the Four Gospels
때가 차매, 영원하신 말씀이 육신을 입고 우리 가운데 거하셨습니다. 예수: When the fullness of time had come, the eternal Word put on flesh and dwelt among us. Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem in the land of Judea, grew up in Nazareth of Galilee, and began His public ministry by receiving baptism from John the Baptist. Through the Sermon on the Mount He proclaimed the new law of the kingdom of God, and by healing the sick and casting out demons He proved that the Messiah's kingdom had come. But as a result of sharply rebuking the hypocrisy and hollow faith of the religious leaders, He was hated and arrested in the garden of Gethsemane. On the cross, the most horrific and yet most gracious altar, He bore the sins of all humanity and died shedding His blood, perfectly fulfilling all the sacrifices and prophecies of the Old Testament. Rising again on the third day, breaking the power of death, Jesus spoke to His disciples for 40 days about the kingdom of God, gave the Great Commission to preach the gospel to the ends of the earth, and then ascended into heaven.
사복음서는 네 명의 기자가 각기 다른 대상과 관점을 가지고 예수님을 입체: The Four Gospels are a grand record in which four writers, each with a different audience and point of view, shed light on Jesus from every side. Matthew, which presents Him to the Jews as the 'King of kings' who fulfilled the Old Testament prophecies; Mark, which portrays Him to the Romans as the 'suffering servant' who worked without rest; Luke, which shows the Greeks the perfect figure of the 'Son of Man (the man)'; and John, which proclaims to the whole universe that Jesus is the 'Son of God' who existed from the beginning! The cross and resurrection of Jesus Christ are the greatest shock ever thrown into history and the perfect conclusion of redemptive history, which runs through the whole Bible as one.
10. 초대교회 & 사도 바울의 선교 (서신서 시대): 10. The Early Church & the Mission of the Apostle Paul (the Age of the Epistles)
오순절 마가의 다락방에 불의 혀처럼 성령이 강림하시면서 폭발적인 초대교회: At Pentecost, as the Holy Spirit came down like tongues of fire on Mark's upper room, the early church was born with explosive force. Through Peter's sermon three thousand people repented and turned back in a single day, but the great persecution that began with Stephen's martyrdom actually became the spark that scattered the gospel into Judea, Samaria, and the Gentile lands. Saul the persecutor, who had tried to destroy the church, met the risen Lord on the road to Damascus and was completely transformed into Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles. Through three missionary journeys he spread the gospel across Asia Minor, Macedonia, and Achaia, all the way to Rome, and planted many Gentile churches. In the process, to set the churches right against countless threats such as the interference of the Judaizers, the temptations of an immoral pagan culture, and division and the infiltration of heresies within the church, he wrote letters with tears, and those are Paul's 13 Epistles. Other apostles such as Peter, James, John, and Jude also left the General Epistles to encourage believers going through fiery trials and persecution and to warn against false teachers.
신약 성경 통독의 성패는 사도행전의 역사적 지리 여정(전도여행 경로) 속: The success or failure of a New Testament read-through depends on whether you can fit Paul's Epistles and the General Epistles in their exact chronological order into the historical and geographical journey of Acts (the routes of the missionary journeys). The anger of Galatians, the tearful appeals of 1 and 2 Corinthians, the joy and cosmic view of the church in the Prison Epistles (Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians), and the Pastoral Epistles, left like a last will to Timothy, his son in the faith, from a pitch-dark prison just before his martyrdom! When you read these letters following Paul's bloodstained footsteps, the wild vitality of the gospel and the true discipleship that the church today must recover come alive.
11. 사도 요한의 묵시 & 새 하늘과 새 땅: 11. The Apostle John's Revelation & the New Heaven and New Earth
로마 제국의 도미티아누스 황제가 자신을 '주와 하나님'으로 숭배할 것을: It was a time of terrible persecution, when the Roman emperor Domitian forced people to worship him as 'Lord and God' and Christians were thrown to wild beasts and burned at the stake. John, the last apostle, who had been the pastor of the church in Ephesus, was exiled to the stone quarries of the island of Patmos. On that island of pitch-dark despair, John, in the Spirit on the Lord's Day, sees through an open door in heaven a vast revelation of the things that are to come. It was not a scare tactic about terrible disasters, but a majestic letter of comfort to suffering believers. Through the judgments of the seven seals, seven trumpets, and seven bowls, the Roman Empire (the harlot Babylon) and the forces of Satan that oppose God will at last be thrown into the lake of fire and suffer eternal destruction. Finally the first heaven and the first earth pass away, and it ends with the glorious vision of the new heaven and new earth, where God Himself pitches His tent and wipes away every tear from His people's eyes, and of the holy city, the New Jerusalem, coming down.
요한계시록은 점쟁이들의 예언서나 이단들의 공갈 협박용 도구가 결코 아닙니: Revelation is never a book of predictions for fortune-tellers or a tool for threats and blackmail by cults! It is the splendid finale of redemptive history, in which the tree of life in the Garden of Eden and the tragedy of paradise lost, lost through the sin of the first man Adam in Genesis, are perfectly restored and completed in Revelation 22 through Jesus Christ, the Lamb. Like the early church believers who never bowed their knees even before the sword of the Roman Empire, it is a great epic of victory that strongly urges us, who compromise with materialism today, to recover the faith of our first love: 'Maranatha, Amen, come, Lord Jesus.'
